This is my first D&D game ever, and I'll be honest: the first ten hours were rough. Turn-based combat, dice rolls, spell slots, advantage and disadvantage, none of it made sense to me at the start. I almost bounced off it.

I'm glad I pushed through. Once the systems click, the core gameplay becomes genuinely addictive. Every fight is a puzzle with ten different solutions. You can talk your way out, sneak past, shove someone off a cliff, or set the ground on fire and watch the chaos. The game reacts to almost everything you try, which is exactly what makes it so hard to put down.

And the amount of content is insane. Three massive acts, companions with real stories, choices that actually matter, and so many ways to build your character and approach every situation that I was planning a second playthrough before finishing my first.

If you've never touched D&D or a CRPG before, don't let that scare you off. The learning curve is real, but it's absolutely worth it. One of the best games I've ever played.

As someone who really likes DND, Baldur's Gate 3 is basically as close to the tabletop as you can get and play digitally. The characters, be it important or minor NPCs are full of personality and the world building is very detailed. While yes, the rules are a bit different to cater to casual fans of the game or people who only got the game due to popularity, it brings a perfect balance of the two.

This game values player's freedom of choice a lot, therefore every playthrough is unique. Consistently runs well with minor to no bugs or issues despite big game size even on lower end devices in rendering the game. Wide range of settings to accommodate all hardware. Built in modding marketplace is already a huge bonus, offering the game even more replayability and fun. The co-op mode is pretty solid.

The combat may not be everyone's thing, as it is turn-based. But it does offer a wide variety of moves and combinations which even are affected by the position of the map and your surroundings, making immersion even better. Difficulty can be changed mid-combat if it ever becomes too hard, which is a nice touch. The combat is a 9/10. Sometimes minor bugs may happen.


The story is great. Gives special interactions and shifts the narrative based on your choices to change the experience. Act 1 is definitely the most memorable, and while Act 2 does get a bit monotone the immense flood of new content in Act 3 makes up for it. I rate the main story an 8/10.

 The game features over 10 days wroth of nonstop voiced dialogue, highly detailed and well-written characters, fun combat mechanics. Good world building. Even if you don't care about that, getting it for the character customization is worth it alone for authors/artists. For characters, most of the ones available to be added to your party are romanceable, which is a good way of learning their individual backstories. These are well-thought out and incorporated into the main story. They also provide more information about the lore.



For the price of the game, it is worth your money. Especially if it goes on sale; it didn't win game of the year for nothing. Very replayable, entertaining. Graphics are good, mechanics are fun, settings accommodating. Characters are well-thought out, full of life, and their own and the main story is well-written. The world is detailed and fun to explore. Highly recommended, 9.5/10 if not 10/10 game.

Finally, I've completed this massive and immersive RPG combined with incredibly fun gameplay with around 150hrs playtime (it's 200ish hrs on Steam cause I did a lot of save scumming and AFK). Now, I get it why this game won GOTY back in 2023. This is the most beginner-friendly CRPG I've played so far, at least compared to DOS2 and Pathfinder WOTR. At first, it really looks very complex and deep, but after playing it for a while turns out its really not that difficult. The character creation is fine, there are a lot of classes and races that we can choose but not that much that it becomes overwhelming like Pathfinder WOTR. You can also multiclass in this game that makes experimenting with builds so much fun, and I'm also thinking you can build a character on your own without looking up builds on the internet without worrying your character doesn't do enough damage.

The thing I liked the most from this game would be the story and the freedom of choices you have. You can be good, evil, or neutral, everything, and every choice you made feels like it has consequences. The companion stories are also memorable, especially Shadowheart and Astarion, also their voice acting is incredible. No wonder Astarion's voice actor won the Best Performance at TGA 2023. For the combat, i think it's not bad although the combat in DOS2 felt more interactive. Anyway, overall I'm very satisfied and the game exceeded my expectations after I've played DOS2. Definitely would play another playthrough, even I've already planned what I'm gonna do in the next playthrough. I'm getting more and more excited for the next Larian Studios' CRPG, Divinity.

I’ve finished Baldur’s Gate 3 and I had a great time. This game is absolutely amazing. A true masterpiece — a gem that’s hard to come across these days. It feels like a game made by gamers, for gamers.

I had never played any of the previous Baldur’s Gate games and I wasn’t familiar with D&D mechanics. I had heard that BG3 was a great game, but I didn’t want to play another game like Divine Divinity, so I kept putting it off for over three years. My friends strongly recommended it, so I finally decided to give it a try.

And what can I say? This game is a masterpiece.

Pros:
- Great graphics
- Great music
- Excellent gameplay
- Engaging story
- No excessive political correctness — the game doesn’t shy away from brutality
- Quite expensive for a three-year-old game, but absolutely worth the money

Cons:
- It does feel a bit like Divinity at times
- Occasional bugs and crashes
- Larian’s approach of putting garbage trash everywhere. Larian’s approach of putting chests, loot, and random junk everywhere means I end up running around like a scrap collector: loot, sell, loot, sell, loot, sell, over and over again.
- By the end of the game, I had several hundred items that I never used 
- I had more money than I could possibly spend

I tend to play games by exploring absolutely everything and collecting everything I can find. While this is fun to some extent, it also takes a lot of time and, in the end, doesn’t really add that much to the experience. It’s great that there are so many hidden items, chests, and secrets, but there is honestly a bit too much of it.

I really, really enjoyed Baldur’s Gate 3. I played Divine Divinity years ago, but I didn’t really understand what was going on in the story back then.

If I had one wish, I’d say it’s a shame that Larian is working on another Divinity game instead of a new Baldur’s Gate. Larian put an enormous amount of work and effort into BG3, and it really shows.

For me, this is a masterpiece — the kind of game that is very hard to find these days. It has some minor bugs and occasional crashes, but those are nothing compared to everything the game does right.

В цій грі є лише три добре зроблені аспекти - це саундтрек, гумор Карлак і задниця Тінесердої. Усе інше в цій грі - суцільна посередність. Технічний стан гри - поганий, в грі велика кількість візуальних і звукових багів. Найбільше дратує постійна необхідність видаляти сейви, бо інакше гра фрізиться кожні декілька секунд. Візуальна складова гри - примітивна. Часто можна помітити відсутність тіні від об'єкта чи різкі стрибки якості деталізації текстур різних предметів.  Деталізована моделька шафи, куплена в магазині асетів, стоїть поруч з моделькою крісла, яку  портували з ванільного WoW - це феномен BG3. Особливої  уваги вигляду і різноманіттю зброї та одягу розрорбники також не приділили,  можете забути про стандартний для індустрії рівень пропрацьованості спорядження у фентезійній грі. Усі гроші пішли на постановку романтичної сцени з Галсіном, тому ось вам 5 мечів, 4 сокири і 3 луки на всю гру. Ще на початку гри я зрозумів, що головними лиходіями у цій грі є сценаристи. Якщо вас зачарували численні високі оціник цієї гри і ви вже очікуєте пройти гру, де сюжетні повороти і драматургія перевершили The Witcher 3, то охолодіть свої очікування, бо сюжет і його подача у гри простенькі. Я так і не зрозумів чому головного героя повинна турбувати доля Орфея та його народу, сценарист просто поставив у 3 акті нас перед фактом. Діалогова система тут десь на рівні Fallout 4, але має неприємну особливість створювати враження відсутності логічного зв'язку між тим, що говорить твій персонаж і як на це реагує співрозмовник. Персонажі. В BG3 мало персонажів, які викликають цікавість чи симпатію і зазвичай ти просто хочеш їх позбутися (привіт Астаріон). Розробникам було настільки байджуе на створення персонажів, що реакцію напарників на вчинки головного героя вони прописали випадковим чином: позитивного персонажа може засмутити ваша позитивна дія. Найбільшою проблемою гри є її посередність у всіх аспектиах. І я зараз не говорю виключно про численні запозичення з  Володаря перснів. Усі декілкьа сотень годин проходження ви будете відчувати, що от цю підземну кузню гномів ви вже бачли у Скайрімі, а от ця пригода з відьмою на болоті підозріло нагадує Відьмака. Сам факт запозичень - це не гріх, але не тоді, коли результат вийшов гіршим, ніж оригінал. Одразу помітно, що розробники не мали власного бачення гри. Вони б джуе хотіли повторити то одну, то іншу гру. Їм справді кортіло мати свою фінуальну битву і вечріку з друзями як в Mass Effect, але маємо те, що маємо: 5/10

I'll start by saying that I'm completely unfamiliar with the world of D&D. My only experience that was at least somewhat related to it was Dragon Age: Origins, which I played quite a while ago, absolutely loved, but I haven't really played many games in the same genre. Still, as soon as I stepped out of the nautiloid at the beginning of Act I, I was hit by that same bittersweet nostalgia for that game, for those characters I loved, for that kind of narrative complexity that you rarely find.

DIFFICULTY

I soon ran into a difficulty I never would have expected from a game like this. For context, I'm the kind of player who is always looking for the perfect balance between "challenge" and "play-for-fun", raising the difficulty above normal only when I start getting a little bored because the combat is too easy. When there's a "story" or "explorer" mode, or whatever it's called, I only touch it in games that are making me suffer so much that I just want to finish them quickly.

Well, this was my one and only exception. Damn it.

After around 140 hours of gameplay, I think I finally started to understand how the game was actually supposed to be played, because combat started to feel a little easier... And that was at the very end of Act III.

Let's just say that the game seems to take for granted that you already have a certain familiarity with this kind of game, and when you don't, it really makes your life difficult.

NARRATIVE

This is where I put all my love.

Beyond the truly billions of variables your story can take, many of which are accounted for by the developers and are absolutely anything but predictable, you're faced with characters who were clearly written with a lot of heart. The complete opposite of bland or formulaic characters, people you genuinely feel like you're forming a bond with.


Shadowheart and Karlach have genuinely found a place in my heart, without taking anything away from the other characters, who are all written just as beautifully.

And now I'm going to spend months stuck in the post-game gaming slump, with absolutely no idea what to play next, fully aware that a masterpiece like this will be very hard to match.

Sigh.

P.S. Larian, I hate you for not putting Karlach on the cover!

About 60% of the game is trudging across the map, solving puzzles designed by someone who confused “obtuse” with “clever,” then backtracking across the same damn wilderness because apparently walking is content now. The other 20% is story, characters, combat, and loot, occasionally appearing like they’re doing the player a favor.

The infuriating part is that the homework was already done. Dragon Age: Origins, KOTOR 2, Mass Effect. Just look at what worked, improve it, and let people actually play the damn RPG. Instead, Larian built a 100-hour group-therapy retreat with dice rolls, stuffed it with fetch quests and environmental busywork, threw some tieflings into the mix, and convinced half the internet that exhaustion is immersion.

It’s not an RPG. It’s a wellness app that occasionally lets you stab a goblin.

Baldur’s Gate 3 to nie jest Baldur’s Gate 3. To Divinity: Original Sin 2 z naklejką „Baldur’s Gate” przyklejoną na siłę, żeby sprzedać więcej kopii.
Dla fana pierwszej części (i trochę drugiej) to jest jakby ktoś wziął grę, którą kochasz za klimat, ciężar, poczucie, że jesteś zwykłym skurwysynem w niebezpiecznym świecie… i zamienił ją w kolorowy, wygadany, romantyczno-komediowy theme park, w którym wszyscy towarzysze to główne postacie z własnymi traumą, seksem i łukami, a ty jesteś tylko tłem do ich fanficów.
W BG1 i BG2 towarzysze byli ludźmi. Czasem debilami, czasem psychami, czasem zwykłymi najemnikami. Tutaj masz gotowe archetypy z TikToka: wampir-suka, jaszczurka-wojowniczka, czarodziej z problemami z ego, panienka z amnezją i ogniem w tyłku. Każdy musi mieć swoją wielką historię, każdy chce się z tobą przespać albo przynajmniej porozmawiać o uczuciach przez pół godziny. Klasyczna drużyna to była banda, która szła z tobą zabijać. Tutaj to grupa terapeutyczna z mieczami.
Klimat? W oryginałach był brud, niebezpieczeństwo, poczucie, że świat cię jebie. Tutaj nawet najciemniejsze momenty są podane z lekkim uśmieszkiem i efektami specjalnymi. Narrator gada jakby czytał audiobooka dla dzieci, a dialogi czasem brzmią jakby pisał je ktoś, kto właśnie skończył oglądać Critical Role i uznał, że „grit” to jak ktoś powie „kurwa”.
Bitwy? Zamiast real-time with pause, które miało swój flow i chaos, dostałeś klasyczne turowce Lariana. Dla niektórych rewelacja, dla fana Infinity Engine to jak zamiana skrzyni biegów na automat. Wolniejsze, bardziej przewidywalne, mniej „jebanie się w realnym czasie”.
A najgorsze? Gra kompletnie wyjebała w kosmos to, co się stało w BG1 i Throne of Bhaal. Bhaalspawn saga? Jakiś przypis. Sarevok, Viconia, Jaheira, Minsc – albo karykatury, albo tło. Gra udaje, że jest kontynuacją, a tak naprawdę jest soft-rebootem, który bierze sobie z serii tylko nazwę, miasto i kilka memów.

[b]Baldur's Gate 3[/b] é um CRPG gigantesco e extremamente ambicioso, capaz de oferecer centenas de horas de conteúdo, inúmeras rotas, escolhas com consequências reais e uma liberdade impressionante para criar personagens, builds e resolver situações das formas mais absurdas possíveis. Foram cerca de 247 horas para completar 100% do jogo, e apesar de toda essa qualidade, o excesso de RNG, alguns bugs, comandos imprecisos e uma reta final menos impactante impedem que a experiência alcance a classificação máxima.

[h3][b]Pros:[/b][/h3]

+ [b]Liberdade de Escolha Impressionante:[/b] O jogo realmente passa a sensação de que o jogador está no controle. Decisões, diálogos, caminhos e ações podem alterar quests, personagens e acontecimentos futuros de maneira significativa.

+ [b]Quantidade Absurda de Conteúdo:[/b] Dividido em três atos, Baldur's Gate 3 possui uma enorme quantidade de missões, áreas, rotas alternativas e situações opcionais. Muito conteúdo pode sequer aparecer em uma única campanha dependendo das escolhas realizadas.

+ [b]Mundo Extremamente Reativo:[/b] Mesmo quando o jogador tenta soluções completamente absurdas, o mundo normalmente consegue reagir de maneira coerente, fazendo parecer que os desenvolvedores realmente pensaram em quase tudo.

+ [b]Excelente Variedade de Personagens:[/b] É possível escolher entre personagens de origem ou criar completamente o próprio protagonista, combinando diferentes raças, classes, subclasses e características. Só a criação de personagem pode consumir horas para quem gosta de experimentar possibilidades.

+ [b]Grande Profundidade de Builds:[/b] O sistema de combate permite criar combinações extremamente poderosas quando o jogador entende bem as mecânicas, habilidades, equipamentos e sinergias entre classes.

+ [b]Diálogos Totalmente Dublados:[/b] A enorme quantidade de conversas do jogo possui dublagem em inglês, demonstrando o enorme nível de produção e cuidado dedicado aos personagens e à narrativa.

+ [b]Boa Variedade de Dificuldade:[/b] Existem diferentes níveis de dificuldade, permitindo adaptar a experiência tanto para jogadores interessados principalmente na história quanto para aqueles que procuram combates muito mais punitivos.

+ [b]Cooperativo Muito Bem Integrado:[/b] O jogo pode ser aproveitado em coop, inclusive com tela dividida, permitindo que jogadores com níveis diferentes de experiência participem juntos da campanha.

+ [b]Excelente Custo-Benefício:[/b] Pela quantidade de conteúdo, possibilidades e centenas de horas de diversão disponíveis, Baldur's Gate 3 entrega uma experiência extremamente completa pelo preço cobrado.

[h3][b]Cons:[/b][/h3]

- [b]RNG Presente em Praticamente Tudo:[/b] Por seguir fortemente as regras de D&D, ataques, defesas, testes de diálogo e diversas outras ações dependem de dados. Mesmo utilizando bônus e criando boas estratégias, uma falha crítica pode destruir um plano simplesmente por azar.

- [b]Save Scumming Quase Incentivado:[/b] Embora teoricamente o jogador devesse aceitar as consequências de suas ações, perder personagens, diálogos ou situações importantes por causa de uma rolagem ruim frequentemente transforma salvar e recarregar constantemente na opção mais conveniente.

- [b]Conteúdo Facilmente Perdível:[/b] Algumas situações dependem de caminhos extremamente específicos. É possível abordar o mesmo personagem por rotas diferentes e somente uma delas ativar determinado diálogo, enquanto as outras iniciam combate imediatamente.

- [b]Bugs Podem Alterar Situações Importantes:[/b] Certos eventos não funcionam exatamente como deveriam dependendo da ordem das ações ou da maneira como o jogador chega até determinado local, tornando algumas partes da campanha mais frustrantes do que deveriam.

- [b]Comandos Truncados:[/b] Em determinadas situações, tentar conversar com um NPC pode acabar selecionando acidentalmente um objeto próximo, fazendo o personagem tentar roubá-lo e criando problemas completamente involuntários.

- [b]Sistema de Roubo Estranho:[/b] Mesmo quando ninguém presencia diretamente o crime, NPCs podem perceber posteriormente que algum objeto desapareceu e confrontar o jogador, inclusive em situações nas quais isso parece logicamente impossível.

- [b]Curva de Aprendizado Elevada:[/b] Para quem não conhece bem D&D ou sistemas semelhantes, classes, habilidades, posicionamento e funcionamento dos combates podem parecer bastante confusos. Nas dificuldades maiores, cometer pequenos erros pode ser extremamente punitivo.

- [b]Romances Pouco Flexíveis:[/b] Apesar da enorme liberdade disponível no restante da aventura, os relacionamentos amorosos acabam parecendo mais limitados e restritivos do que o restante dos sistemas sociais do jogo.

- [b]Narrativa Perde Força na Reta Final:[/b] A jornada começa extremamente forte, mas perde parte do impacto narrativo ao longo da campanha. O encerramento não consegue ser tão épico quanto tudo que aconteceu anteriormente, especialmente quando comparado a séries como Mass Effect e Dragon Age.

[h3][b]Final Rating: A[/b][/h3]

I rarely write reviews on games, but I felt guilty NOT doing so for what this game is and means to me.

I’m sitting here looking at this blank text box, genuinely struggling to find words that do this masterpiece justice. I’ve put countless hours into RPGs over the years, but what Larian Studios has achieved here isn’t just impressive—it’s historical. A milestone for other devs and companies to aim for. It has to be the new standard after all these years of greedy corporate games. Baldur’s Gate 3 for me is, plain and simple, one of the greatest role-playing games ever created.

So let me give you an overview across different categories, for those who still haven't bought it (INSERT JUST DO IT MEME HERE) or who just want to read the experience of a guy who is deeply in love with this game. Just a small reminder: English is not my main language, so please excuse any minor spelling or grammar mistakes. At least it’s AI-free and written straight from the heart. I literally took 30 minutes to write and think about how to word it.

[list]
[*] [b]Story & Narrative (100% Spoiler-Free):[/b]
The narrative pulls you in from the very first minute. Every reaction, decision, and action can and will impact the story, the characters, and sometimes even the world itself. A lot of RPGs only give you the illusion of choice, but in BG3, your decisions actually carry real weight.

Sure, you can't change EVERYTHING in the game, but you have an insane amount of freedom. Are you going to be good, evil, or somewhere within the 100 shades of grey in between? Which path will you follow? Depending on how you act, your relationships with companions evolve organically, shift radically, or fall apart entirely. It never feels like you're just following a rigid script; you're actively shaping your own unique journey. The replayability is off the charts.

Also, this might be the first RPG where I didn't skip even the minor dialogue because it’s so immensely well-written. The cutscenes are top-notch, and the tabletop Pen-and-Paper feel makes it even more immersive. My personal advice: DO NOT QUICKSAVE/QUICKLOAD every "bad" die roll! You will be so much more immersed if you just live with the consequences. (Sure, on your first run you might want specific outcomes, but trust me on this tip.) Furthermore, EVERY character is exceptionally designed and written—down to the smallest NPC.

[*] [b]Unrivaled Creativity & Character Building:[/b]
If you love theorycrafting and tweaking mechanics, this game is absolute heaven. The character creation and build variety are insanely deep, but what really sets BG3 apart is how much freedom it gives you to solve problems.

There are virtually no artificial walls holding back your ingenuity. If you sit there thinking, [i]"Wait, can I actually use this spell, combine it with the environment, and bypass this entire scenario?"[/i]—almost every single time, the game lets you do it. Whether you're fine-tuning synergies between classes, talking your way out of situations that look like guaranteed fights, or coming up with completely unhinged tactical maneuvers, the game constantly respects your intelligence. It never forces you into one "correct" way to play; it gives you a massive toolbox and lets you go wild. (And trust me, I spent 20% of my playtime in character creation planning and testing builds. Call me an addict.)

[*] [b]Soundtrack & Atmosphere:[/b]
The audio design and world-building are on a completely different level. Borislav Slavov put together a soundtrack that literally stays in your head for weeks.

What makes it so good is how seamlessly the music shifts with the mood. One minute you’re sitting at a quiet campfire talking to your companions with a soft, melancholic melody in the background, and the next you’re thrown into a massive boss battle with full orchestral power and vocals that give you absolute chills. Every region feels distinct, every fight has impact, and the sound design carries the emotional weight of the game perfectly. MAN... that first big fight in the tutorial with that track blasting? HOLY GOOSEBUMPS. Everything is PEAK quality: Music, Voice Acting, Ambience—everything.

[*] [b]Graphics & Visual Presentation:[/b]
Visually, this game is a massive step up for the genre. Top-down RPGs often struggle to feel cinematic, but BG3 completely changes the game with its close-up cutscenes and facial animations. Sure, it’s not mind-blowing UE5 ultra-next-gen graphics, but it looks fantastic, and there are great texture mods available if you want even more crispness.

The attention to detail in the world design is insane—from the dynamic lighting hitting dense forests to the intricate armor textures and spell effects popping off in combat. Even subtle character expressions during dialogue carry emotional weight, making every conversation feel like a high-budget cinematic experience rather than just reading lines of text.

[*] [b]Moddability & Personalization:[/b]
Even in its vanilla state, BG3 is a masterpiece, but the modding potential takes this game straight into infinite replayability territory. Larian backing official mod integration—alongside the insane work the community does on third-party tools—makes customizing your experience seamless.

I’ve personally sunk countless hours into building, testing, and fine-tuning my own custom mod list just to get the mechanics, visual fidelity, and difficulty balancing exactly where I want them. It’s gotten to the point where the guys in my Discord literally started calling me the "Mod Father."

That said, a quick word of advice: curate with care. The modding scene is massive, which means for every incredible quality-of-life tweak, immersive spell pack, or tactical overhaul, there are plenty of cringey, immersion-breaking mods out there that ruin the atmosphere. But if you take the time to build a clean, grounded setup, you can turn an already legendary RPG into your own tailored masterpiece.

[*] [b]Final Verdict & Studio Trust:[/b]
Look, I know how this sounds. Reading through all of this, you might think I’m just some blind Larian fanboy who hypes up anything they drop. I’m really not. I’ve been gaming for way too long, and I’m usually the first person to criticize studios when they get lazy or greedy.

The reality is that BG3 simply earned every single bit of praise it gets. Larian gave haters and cynical critics zero room to hit them with legitimate bashing. In an era where the industry is clogged with half-baked releases, predatory microtransactions, battle passes, and empty live-service promises, Larian (alongside CD Projekt Red) stands as one of the very few AAA studios left that I actually trust. You can feel the sheer love, sweat, and respect for the player packed into every single frame of this game.
[/list]

[b]Final Words:[/b]
